bibliography.title: Comparative biomechanical analyses of lower cervical spine post anterior fusion versus intervertebral disc arthroplasty: A geometrically patient-specific poroelastic finite element investigation

study.research_problem: ACDF, Bryan disc arthroplasty, and Prestige LP arthroplasty alter adjacent-segment mechanics differently, but single-geometry and static FE studies underrepresent anatomical variability and time-dependent disc fluid-solid behavior.
study.exact_gap: Existing cervical FE studies often use one geometry and static loading, rarely combining multiple patient geometries with poroelastic cyclic simulations to compare fusion and two arthroplasty designs (S002:C03-S002:C04).
study.objective_or_hypothesis: Use ten geometrically patient-specific C3-C7 poroelastic models to compare preoperative, ACDF, Bryan, and Prestige LP conditions under static rotations and cyclic follower loading, focusing on ROM, IDP, FJF, disc height/fluid loss, annulus stress, and fiber strain (S001:C01-S002:C04).
study.study_design: Ten parametric FE geometries derived from lateral/AP radiographs were each converted into one preoperative and three simulated postoperative models, yielding 10 intact and 30 treatment models; within-geometry outcomes were compared with Friedman/Nemenyi tests (S004:C01-S005:C03).
study.sample_or_model: Ten patients eligible for C5-C6 ACDF or arthroplasty supplied 28 geometric parameters plus disc height/lordosis; all models shared literature-based material properties, ligament definitions, contact laws, implant catalogue dimensions, and loads (S004:C01-S005:C02).
comparators: C5-C6 ACDF with PEEK cage and bone graft
C5-C6 Prestige LP metal-on-metal artificial disc
Within each patient geometry, not observed postoperative clinical cohorts
method_spine: Extract geometric parameters from AP/lateral radiographs and generate parametric C3-C7 anatomy.
Assign poro-hyperelastic discs/endplates/bone, fiber reinforcement, ligaments, facet contact, and literature material properties.
Check mesh independence and benchmark intact ROM/neutral IDP against external in-vitro ranges.
Modify C5-C6 into ACDF, Bryan, and Prestige scenarios with simplified catalogue implant geometries and tied bone-device interfaces.
Precondition, apply 11000 cyclic follower-load cycles and six separate 1 Nm rotations, and compare biomechanical outputs within geometry.
Keep predicted mechanical surrogates separate from clinical ASD and treatment efficacy.

verification: A meshing sensitivity study selected approximately 52,723 elements with 0.6 mm global edge length, and the Results state that mesh independence was checked (S004:C04; S006:C01).
The packet does not report mesh alternatives, convergence tolerances, solver/time-step checks, mass/energy balance, or poroelastic numerical convergence details.
calibration: No patient-specific material or load calibration is reported; tissue and device properties come from literature/catalogues and all patients share the same mechanics (S004:C02-S004:C05; S007:C08).
The 30-minute preconditioning and fixed pore-pressure boundary mitigate initial swelling but are modeling choices rather than calibration to each patient (S005:C01-S005:C02).
validation: Intact intersegmental ROM under 1 Nm and neutral IDP under 100 N were within external cadaveric literature ranges; axial rotation at C3-C4 was a notable mismatch (S004:C06; S006:C01; S007:C01-S007:C02).

Agreement with an earlier geometrically accurate model supports face/trend plausibility, but no independent postoperative experiment or patient outcome validates ACDF/Bryan/Prestige predictions (S007:C02).
sensitivity: Ten geometries expose anatomical variability and within-geometry reversals between Bryan and Prestige, which is a useful population-geometry robustness analysis (S007:C06).

No sensitivity or uncertainty analysis varies material properties, permeability, swelling pressure, facet geometry/contact, friction, muscle forces, interface tie, implant placement, load magnitude/direction, or cycle history.
application_prediction: ROM, IDP, FJF, height/fluid loss, annulus stress, and fiber strain are application predictions under specified models; using them for individual surgical planning requires patient-specific inputs and prospective validation not provided here (S008:C01).

primary_outcomes: ACDF markedly reduced C5-C6 ROM and increased adjacent-level ROM during flexion/extension relative to intact and arthroplasty models; axial-rotation differences were less consistent (S006:C01-S006:C02).

Adjacent-level IDP and FJF increased after ACDF during sagittal motion, while Prestige LP produced a comparatively high instrumented-level FJF consistent with modeled hypermobility (S006:C02-S006:C03; S007:C06).

After 11000 cycles, ACDF predicted more adjacent disc-height loss, fluid loss, annulus stress, and fiber strain than arthroplasty; Bryan produced the lowest height/fluid changes in this setup (S006:C03-S006:C04).

Patient geometries showed substantial dispersion and even reversed Bryan-versus-Prestige adjacent-ROM ranking for some patients, demonstrating that group-average direction is not universally individual (S007:C06).
study.highest_evidence_level_reached: Verified and externally benchmarked comparative FE predictions across ten patient geometries; no patient-specific material calibration, postoperative validation, biological degeneration measurement, or clinical ASD outcome.

argument_map.central_claim: Under the specified poroelastic FE assumptions, ACDF transfers more motion/load/fluid-loss surrogates to adjacent segments than two arthroplasty designs, while Bryan best preserves modeled adjacent-disc poroelastic behavior and Prestige may elevate instrumented-level facet force; these are comparative mechanical predictions, not proof of clinical ASD or superior outcomes.
data: Ten intact and thirty treatment FE models, literature-benchmarked intact ROM/IDP, 11000-cycle poroelastic simulations, and within-geometry comparisons of seven mechanical outputs (S004:C01-S006:C04).
Geometry-related interpatient dispersion and model-specific response reversals (S007:C02; S007:C06).
argument_map.warrant: Altered motion, pressure, facet load, fluid exchange, and annulus stress/strain are mechanically plausible pathways toward adjacent-disc degeneration, but each link to biological degeneration and clinical ASD remains inferential.
backing: External cadaveric ROM/IDP ranges support intact-model behavior, and prior literature connects disc height/hydration changes with ASD-related imaging (S004:C06; S007:C04-S007:C07).
argument_map.qualifier: Comparative trend under ten geometries and a fixed parameter/load/interface set.
rebuttals_or_boundaries: Patient specificity applies chiefly to geometry; material, permeability, ligaments, implants, loads, and boundary conditions are not individualized (S004:C01-S004:C05; S007:C08).
Complete osseointegration is imposed with tied contact for all devices, eliminating interface micromotion, subsidence, migration, and fixation failure (S005:C01; S007:C03).
Validation uses intact literature ROM/IDP, not independent postoperative treatment-specific data.
A 11000-cycle 0.5 Hz scenario is estimated from 19 km of walking and is not a multi-year physiological load spectrum (S005:C02; S007:C04-S007:C05).
Follower load omits active muscles and each rotation is simulated separately; implant geometry and facets are simplified (S004:C02-S004:C04; S005:C01-S005:C02; S007:C08-S007:C09).
Mechanical ASD surrogates cannot establish clinical degeneration incidence, symptoms, revision, or quality of life.

measured: AP/lateral radiographic geometric parameters from ten patients and external experimental ROM/IDP benchmark ranges (S004:C01; S004:C06).
predicted: All treatment-specific ROM, IDP, FJF, disc height/fluid loss, annulus stress, and collagen-fiber strain values are FE predictions (S005:C02-S006:C04).
The modeled response assumes fixed C7, follower compression, separate 1 Nm moments, uniform material properties, simplified implants, and perfect device-bone ties.
inferred: Higher adjacent-level predicted metrics after ACDF are interpreted as higher ASD risk, and lower Bryan metrics as better preservation/clinical efficacy (S007:C05-S008:C01).
Prestige FJF is attributed to modeled hypermobility, a plausible internal mechanism not clinically verified here (S007:C06).
recommended: For planning claims, add patient-specific tissue/load calibration, independent postoperative validation, interface and subsidence models, uncertainty propagation, realistic multi-activity loading, and prospective association with ASD endpoints.
proxy_to_outcome_bridges: Predicted ROM/IDP/FJF are mechanical surrogates, not observed degeneration.
Predicted disc height/fluid loss over 11000 cycles is not longitudinal MRI hydration loss or clinical ASD.
Annulus stress/fiber strain suggests a mechanical pathway but does not model inflammation, remodeling, pain, or failure thresholds.
Tied interfaces assume integration rather than predict it.
Within-model statistical significance is not clinical effect or validation.
overclaim_risks: The abstract/conclusion says ACDF poses the highest risk and Bryan shows most efficacy, language stronger than treatment-specific validation supports (S001:C01-S001:C02; S008:C01).
The discussion states artificial disc arthroplasty has better clinical outcomes, although the study contains no postoperative patient outcomes (S007:C07).
The claim that 11000 cycles generalize to long-term responses exceeds the modeled duration and load diversity (S007:C05).
Calling the models patient-specific without the modifier 'geometrically' can conceal uniform materials, loads, and implant assumptions.

section_moves.move: Decompose patient specificity by input class
section_moves.execution: The paper explicitly derives anatomy from 28 radiographic parameters while assigning common literature materials, contacts, implants, and loads (S004:C01-S005:C02).
section_moves.transferable_principle: State separately whether geometry, material, boundary/load, implant, contact, pathology, and calibration are patient-specific; never use the label as an undifferentiated property.
section_moves.failure_mode: Geometry-specific models are not fully patient-specific predictions.

section_moves.move: Keep verification, calibration, validation, and application prediction separate
section_moves.execution: Mesh independence checks numerical discretization, intact ROM/IDP comparison benchmarks model behavior, no calibration is reported, and postoperative outputs are applications (S004:C04-S006:C01).
section_moves.transferable_principle: Write FE credibility as four explicit subsections and identify which data were used in each; intact benchmarking does not validate every postoperative prediction.
section_moves.failure_mode: A model within a literature range is not automatically validated for device ranking or clinical risk.

section_moves.move: Show distribution and individual trend reversals, not only the mean
section_moves.execution: The discussion notes substantial standard deviations and opposite Bryan-versus-Prestige ordering in subsets of the ten geometries (S007:C06).
section_moves.transferable_principle: For virtual cohorts, report per-subject paired effects, dispersion, rank reversals, and the percentage sharing the average direction.
section_moves.failure_mode: A group mean device ranking may not apply to an individual.

section_moves.move: Translate modeled surrogates through an explicit causal chain
section_moves.execution: The paper links rigidity to adjacent load sharing, fluid loss, solid-phase stress/strain, and possible degeneration (S007:C05-S007:C07).
section_moves.transferable_principle: Write each FE-to-clinical inference as predicted mechanical change, hypothesized biological consequence, missing validation link, and bounded clinical implication.
section_moves.failure_mode: Do not call a predicted surrogate a clinical outcome.

section_moves.move: Name scope-defining assumptions rather than generic simplifications
section_moves.execution: The authors identify parametric geometry, shared materials, and omitted active muscle forces; additional key assumptions include tied integration and simplified load history (S007:C08-S007:C09).
section_moves.transferable_principle: For each simplification, state which output it may bias, in what direction if known, and which conclusion must be narrowed.
section_moves.failure_mode: Listing assumptions without propagating them into claim scope is incomplete.

author_reported: Simplified parametric geometry, identical material properties across patients, omitted active muscle forces, simple swelling boundary, and non-lifetime cyclic loading (S007:C04-S007:C09).
reader_identified: No patient-specific material/load calibration and no treatment-specific independent validation.
Perfect device-bone ties preclude osseointegration failure, micromotion, subsidence, and migration.
Simplified catalogue implant geometries and standard heights may not reproduce surgical placement or individual sizing.
Mesh sensitivity is asserted without convergence data and no time-step/poroelastic numerical verification is shown.
Facet geometry, friction/contact, permeability, swelling pressure, ligament properties, and load spectrum lack uncertainty analysis.
Ten patients are a small geometry sample and demographics/pathology do not enter material or loading models.
No biological remodeling, longitudinal imaging, symptoms, ASD events, revision, or patient-reported outcomes.
likely_bias_direction: Perfect fixation and standardized implants may understate interface- and placement-related differences.
Fixed assumptions can make device rankings appear more precise and general than parameter uncertainty permits.
FE-to-clinical language likely overstates ASD and efficacy conclusions.
limitations.scope_boundary: The study compares short-horizon poroelastic mechanical responses of four modeled states across ten geometries; it does not predict individual clinical ASD, validate device integration, establish long-term durability, or demonstrate clinical superiority.

writing_capability_candidates.capability: Decompose 'patient-specific' FE models into geometry, material, load/boundary, implant/contact, pathology, and calibration dimensions.
writing_capability_candidates.manuscript_use: Methods, model table, title/abstract wording, and limitations.
writing_capability_candidates.counterexample_or_boundary: Patient-specific geometry with common materials and loads is geometrically patient-specific, not a fully individualized prediction.

writing_capability_candidates.capability: Classify FE evidence explicitly as verification, calibration, validation, sensitivity, or application prediction and prevent role substitution.
writing_capability_candidates.manuscript_use: Computational Methods, credibility table, Results, and Discussion.
writing_capability_candidates.counterexample_or_boundary: Intact literature-range ROM/IDP does not validate postoperative device rankings or ASD risk.

writing_capability_candidates.capability: Report virtual-cohort mean effects together with subject-level dispersion and rank reversals, then bridge mechanical surrogate to clinical outcome in labeled steps.
writing_capability_candidates.manuscript_use: FE Results figures and Discussion causal chain.
writing_capability_candidates.counterexample_or_boundary: A mean Bryan advantage does not hold for every geometry, and lower surrogates do not prove lower clinical ASD incidence.

critical_weaknesses: Only geometry is individualized; parameter and load uncertainty is not propagated.
Perfect integration and no treatment-specific validation.
Long-term ASD and clinical efficacy language exceeds the simulated evidence.

summary_zh: 这是真正的患者几何特异性孔弹性有限元研究：10 名患者的 X 线参数生成 C3–C7 几何，每个几何比较术前、ACDF、Bryan 和 Prestige LP，共 40 个模型。网格独立性与术前 ROM/IDP 文献范围提供 verification/外部 benchmark，但材料、载荷、接触和植入物并未个体化，也没有用独立术后实验或患者数据验证三种手术预测。模型把器械与骨完全 tie，等于预先假定完全骨整合；11000 次、0.5 Hz 的载荷约对应一次 19 km 步行，不代表多年负载史。ACDF 的邻近节段 ROM、IDP、FJF、流体/高度损失和环纤维应力应写为 predicted mechanical surrogates，不能直接写成临床 ASD。Skill 将据此强制拆分‘患者特异’维度，并严格区分 verification、calibration、validation、sensitivity 和 application prediction。
reader_notes: Primary Codex reader reviewed every non-reference packet section, including all model equations/properties, contacts, loads, outcomes, validation comparison, and limitations.
The article is computational; experimental and clinical content is limited to external benchmark data and source imaging.
The strongest reusable features are FE evidence-role separation and virtual-cohort dispersion; the main counterexample is proxy-to-clinical overreach.
